generic_sampling_rules.integer_pk: Sequential integers starting at max(compact)+1; unique per table; never NULL; for composite PKs generate tuples that do not collide with pre-existing compact tuples; never apply aggregate/group/dup transforms to PK columns.
generic_sampling_rules.integer_fk: Draw from the parent table's FINAL key pool (compact + generated, after all parent-side dedup/PK assignment); never NULL for NOT NULL FK columns; for nullable FK columns ~10% NULL (>=1 row per instance). At least one parent PK value is excluded from the draw pool per (parent, child-FK) pair so it stays childless in that child table. FK values are filled AFTER parent keys are final and are never overwritten by later re-planting; if a later step must change an FK column, re-fill from the final parent pool. FK columns are populated in a dedicated fill phase that runs after all non-FK columns exist; the row count for a table whose columns are all FKs (e.g. follows) is taken from table_sizes_per_instance, not from any column array.
generic_sampling_rules.integer_numeric: Uniform integer in [min,max] from statistics; plant each listed boundary literal and one step on each side; boundary literals are guaranteed to appear (not probabilistic).
generic_sampling_rules.varchar_text: Short strings; for LIKE columns plant the exact literal, a prefix variant, a case variant, and one near variant (~30% of fresh rows carry a planted match); literals are per-column (see per_column_exceptions), never a global default.
generic_sampling_rules.char_text: Padded to declared length; plant exact and near-variant matches for LIKE literals; length <= declared length.
generic_sampling_rules.datetime: Random timestamps within the column's declared range (see semantic rules); force at least two rows to share one timestamp (tie) for ORDER columns; NULL ~10% for nullable date columns.
generic_sampling_rules.null_share: For nullable columns ~10% NULL (>=1 row per column per instance); plant NULLs after all dedup/filter steps; never NULL primary keys or NOT NULL columns; a planted NULL is never replaced to satisfy a rule.
generic_sampling_rules.duplicates: For distinct-share columns target 20-50% duplicate share among non-null rows; verify post-write and adjust by adding/removing duplicates; never apply to primary-key columns.

semantic_rules_and_formulas.evidence: compact createdate values 2018-03-09 20:00:14, 2018-03-12 02:30:30 fall in 2018; rule is inferred from two compact values and marked uncertain

generation_specification.uncertainty: No calculated columns and no date pairs exist; createdate range rule is inferred from two compact values (2018) and is marked uncertain (not a hard constraint). NULL shares estimated at ~10% for nullable columns; compact rows kept and never deleted or modified. table_sizes_per_instance is a fixed per-instance size (8/9/10); the program must generate exactly these counts and ensure per-column targets remain achievable at that size. Sampling must plant NULLs, ties, duplicates, group-size histograms, boundary literals and childless parents on the FINAL arrays after dedup and FK fill; FK columns are filled from the final parent key pool and never overwritten by later re-planting; follows composite PK collisions must be avoided against compact tuples in the plan before insert. The follows table has only FK columns; its row count must come from table_sizes_per_instance and its column dict must be initialized empty before FK fill. Aggregate/group/dup transforms must never be applied to primary-key columns (tweets.id, user_profiles.uid). The f2 domain {-1,1} conflicts with the FK reference to user_profiles.uid; resolution: ensure user_profiles.uid includes -1 and 1 so the f2 pool restricted to {-1,1} is nonempty and both values appear. Post-write verification must confirm: every non-NULL FK value exists in the parent table; at least one parent has zero children in tweets.uid and at least one has zero children in follows.f1 (independently); child-count histogram contains 1, 2 and >=3; f2 subset of {-1,1} with both present; followers contains 999/1000/1001; createdate ties within 2018; duplicate shares 20-50% on email and tweets.uid; followers-per-partition distinct values. Fail the unit or replant on non-FK columns only when a target is unmet.

issues.evidence: writer.write_instance_sqlite is called from cli._one as `write_instance_sqlite(_G['schema'], inst, p)` with no `orig` argument, so it takes the `orig is None` branch and builds an empty DDL clone instead of copying the compact database. Execution feedback confirms this: validity.reasons shows `compact_rows_missing: 20` for all 20 instances, and `no_rows_added: 18` (only 2 instances had any rows survive). The docstring and module header both claim 'Each instance is a copy of the compact database plus appended generated rows', but the code path never does that.
issues.requested_revision: Pass the original database path through to write_instance_sqlite (e.g. `write_instance_sqlite(_G['schema'], inst, p, orig=_G['orig'])` and store `orig` in `_G` in `_init`/`main`), so `_copy_compact` runs and compact rows are preserved. Re-run and confirm `compact_rows_missing` is 0 and `rows_added` is non-zero for every instance.

issues.evidence: rows_skipped is very high: follows 69 skipped vs 48 added, tweets 128 skipped vs 63 added. The writer inserts generated rows with `pragma foreign_keys = OFF` and no dedup against compact rows, so PK collisions with compact rows (e.g. follows (f1,f2) pairs, tweets.id) are silently dropped. Because generated PKs start above the compact max (`_fresh_pk_start`) but FK values are drawn from the parent pool including compact values, composite PKs in `follows` collide with existing compact pairs. This means the intended group-size / aggregate-boundary / duplicate-share targets are not actually realized in the written instance.
issues.requested_revision: Either (a) generate `follows` pairs that avoid existing compact (f1,f2) tuples, or (b) count and report collisions explicitly and ensure the surviving rows still satisfy the per-column targets (group sizes 1/2/>=3, COUNT values 0..3, 20-50% duplicate share). Verify with a post-write check that the targets hold on the final instance, not just on the pre-insert column arrays.

issues.evidence: The NULL rule is not met for several nullable columns. Execution feedback: `user_profiles.followers: NULL 0 / 2`, `user_profiles.name: NULL 0 / 2`, `user_profiles.partitionid: NULL 0 / 2`, `user_profiles.email: NULL 1 / 2`. The spec's `null_targets` lists all of these as nullable, and the interface rule requires at least one NULL row per nullable column per instance. `_plant_nulls` is applied, but the subsequent `sample_fresh_primary_keys` / `drop_unique_duplicates` / FK re-fill steps and the writer's row-skipping can drop the NULL rows, and for `user_profiles` the generated row count is only 2 (base 7 * (0.5..2.0) rounded), so a single NULL is easily lost.
issues.requested_revision: Guarantee at least one NULL survives to the written instance for every nullable column: apply `_plant_nulls` after all filtering/dedup steps, or re-plant a NULL if the post-filter column has none. Also ensure the per-instance row count is large enough (>= 2) that a NULL share of ~10% yields at least one NULL. Re-run and confirm every nullable column shows NULL >= 1 / n.

issues.evidence: `_apply_agg_boundary` is a no-op: the loop body only contains a comment and `pass`-like logic (`for k, tgt in enumerate(sorted(targets)): if tgt <= 0 or k >= n: continue` with no assignment). The spec requires COUNT(*) values 0,1,2,3 for `user_profiles.uid`, `tweets.uid`, `tweets.id`, `user_profiles.partitionid`. Similarly `_apply_group_sizes` overwrites the first `sum(targets)` positions with a single base value per target size, which does not reliably produce groups of sizes 1, 2 and >=3 across the column (it produces one block of each size, but the surrounding values may merge with them).
issues.requested_revision: Implement `_apply_agg_boundary` to actually construct the required COUNT distribution (e.g. partition rows into groups whose sizes hit 0,1,2,3 for the relevant aggregate), and make `_apply_group_sizes` produce a multiset whose group-size histogram contains 1, 2 and >=3 without accidental merging. Add a post-write assertion that the targets hold on the final instance.

issues.evidence: `_childless_parents` returns a random index set, and the FK re-fill sets blocked parent keys to NULL in the child column. But the spec's `unmatched_join_rows` target is 'parent rows without children' — i.e. a parent row that exists but has no child rows. Setting the child FK to NULL does not create a childless parent; it creates a child with a NULL FK. The correct construction is to ensure some parent PK value is never referenced by any child row. The current code also only blocks one random parent per FK, and only if `(t,c)` is in `unmatched_parents`, which is populated from `per_column_exceptions` with pattern `unmatched_join_rows` — but the spec lists this pattern for `user_profiles.uid`, `tweets.uid`, `follows.f1`, not for the child FK columns.
issues.requested_revision: Rework childless-parent construction: after generating all child rows, pick at least one parent PK value per FK that is not present in the child FK column (and not NULL), and ensure it stays unreferenced. Do not achieve 'unmatched' by nulling child FKs. Verify with a post-write query that at least one parent row has zero children for each FK.

issues.evidence: The specification's `semantic_rules_and_formulas` includes `tweets.createdate: createdate IS NOT NULL OR createdate IS NULL`, which is a tautology and provides no constraint. `formula_kind` maps it to 'nullable', which is harmless but meaningless. The `supporting_evidence` for this rule is absent (only uid, followers, id, f2, text have evidence). The `uncertainty` field acknowledges 'createdate has no paired end date' but the rule is still listed.
issues.requested_revision: Remove the tautological `createdate` formula or replace it with a meaningful constraint (e.g. a plausible date range). If no constraint is intended, drop it from `semantic_rules_and_formulas` so the spec does not claim a rule that is not enforced.

issues.evidence: The spec's `per_column_exceptions` lists `unmatched_join_rows` for `user_profiles.uid`, `tweets.uid`, `follows.f1` with target 'parent rows without children', but the atomic-operations extraction shows the actual join predicates are `JOIN(tweets.uid=user_profiles.uid)` and `JOIN(follows.f1=user_profiles.uid)`. The spec does not state which side is the parent for each join, and `follows.f1` is itself a child of `user_profiles.uid`, so 'parent rows without children' for `follows.f1` is ambiguous (follows has no children in the schema). This ambiguity is what led the engineer to implement it as NULL-ing child FKs.
issues.requested_revision: Clarify in the spec, for each `unmatched_join_rows` exception, which table is the parent and which is the child, and state that the target is 'a parent PK value not referenced by any child FK value'. Remove `follows.f1` from the list if it has no children, or restate the target for it.

issues.evidence: `choose_table_sizes` uses `spec['table_sizes']` as a base and multiplies by `0.5 + rng.random() * 1.5`, so `user_profiles` (base 7) yields 3..14 rows, `tweets` (base 8) yields 4..16, `follows` (base 9) yields 4..18. With such small sizes, the per-column targets (group sizes 1/2/>=3, COUNT 0..3, 20-50% duplicate share, NULL share) are frequently unachievable or lost to row-skipping. The execution feedback shows only 2 generated rows for `user_profiles` in some instances.
issues.requested_revision: Either fix the per-instance size to the spec's `table_sizes_per_instance` (7/8/9) or raise the minimum so the targets are achievable, and add a post-write check that each per-column target is satisfied. If a target cannot be satisfied at the chosen size, increase the size rather than silently dropping rows.

issues.evidence: `_apply_duplicates` picks a random non-null index and copies another non-null value into it, but does not guarantee the resulting duplicate share is in 20-50% of non-null rows; it copies `round(len(nonnull) * share)` values, which can over- or under-shoot after subsequent filtering. The spec requires 20-50% duplicate share for `user_profiles.uid`, `tweets.uid`, `user_profiles.email`. No post-write verification is performed.
issues.requested_revision: After all filtering, compute the actual duplicate share and adjust (add or remove duplicates) to land in 20-50%. Add a post-write check that reports the achieved share per column.

issues.evidence: `_constraints_for` sets `cons['ties']` from `schema.original_values` for `ties_order` columns, but `DateSampler.sample` returns a tie value with probability 0.30 only when `self.ties` is non-empty. If the compact `tweets.createdate` values are all distinct (likely), the ties list is non-empty but the generated rows may not actually produce ties at the ORDER BY rank. The spec requires 'ties at rank, ASC' for `tweets.createdate`. No post-write check verifies ties exist.
issues.requested_revision: Guarantee at least two generated rows share the same `createdate` value (e.g. force a duplicate timestamp among generated rows), and add a post-write check that the ORDER BY `createdate` ASC has at least one tie.

unresolved_checks: Whether the compact database actually contains rows for all three tables (the execution feedback reports compact_rows_missing for all 20 instances, which is consistent with the writer bug but could also indicate an empty compact DB; the reviewer cannot inspect the compact DB directly).
Whether the `follows` composite PK collisions are the sole cause of the high rows_skipped, or whether other constraints (e.g. NOT NULL on `tweets.text`) also contribute.

Whether the `tweets.text` LIKE variants (`%int%`, `%intern%`, and the listed near variants) are actually present in the written instances; the StringSampler plants them with probability 0.30, but row-skipping may remove them.

Whether the `follows.f2 <> 0` boundary values (-1, 0, 1) are actually generated; `NumberSampler` pins boundary values with probability 0.25, but the spec's `comparison_boundary` for `follows.f2` is set from `DEFAULT_COMPARISON_BOUNDARY = (-1, 0, 1)`, and the formula `f2 <> 0` is enforced via `nonzero`, which would reject 0 — a conflict between the boundary target and the formula that is not resolved in the code.

issues.evidence: Execution feedback reports fk_violations=109 across 20 instances (integrity.fk_violations), and validity shows 18/20 instances invalid with reason 'new_integrity_failures'. The writer disables FK enforcement (writer.py: con.execute('pragma foreign_keys = OFF')) and the instance builder nulls out blocked childless-parent keys (instance.py: inst[ct][cc] = [v if v not in blocked else None ...]) and re-fills FKs with rng.choice(pv) without re-checking that the chosen parent key still exists after sample_fresh_primary_keys/drop_unique_duplicates on the parent. The post-build _post_verify then re-plants NULLs/duplicates/group sizes on FK columns, which can overwrite a valid FK with a value not present in the parent (e.g. _apply_group_sizes/_apply_agg_boundary/_enforce_dup_share on tweets.uid, follows.f1).
issues.requested_revision: Guarantee FK integrity on the final column arrays: (a) do not run group_sizes/agg_values/dup_share/ties re-planting on FK child columns after FK fill, or re-fill FKs after every re-plant; (b) when nulling blocked childless-parent keys, ensure the resulting NULL is allowed (nullable FK) and that non-NULL values still reference an existing parent key; (c) keep foreign_keys=OFF only for insertion order, but add a post-write verification that every non-NULL FK value exists in the parent table and fail the unit otherwise. Re-run and confirm fk_violations=0 and validity.invalid=0.

issues.evidence: The specification requires (per_column_exceptions) for tweets.uid unmatched_join_rows: 'child FK column contains no reference to >=1 parent (user_profiles.uid); do NOT implement by nulling child FK'. The program implements childless parents by nulling the child FK (instance.py: inst[ct][cc] = [v if v not in blocked else None for v in inst[ct][cc]]), which is exactly the forbidden implementation and also produces the FK violations above. Additionally, _childless_parents only registers a childless parent for columns in spec['unmatched_parents'], but load_specification adds (t,c) for the *child* column (tweets.uid, follows.f1), while _childless_parents is called on parent PK columns (user_profiles.uid) — the key never matches, so childless parents are effectively never enforced.
issues.requested_revision: Implement unmatched_join_rows by leaving at least one parent PK value unreferenced by any child row (choose a parent key and exclude it from the FK draw pool), never by nulling the child FK. Fix the key mismatch: map the spec's child-column entry to the parent PK column before calling _childless_parents, and verify post-write that at least one parent row has zero children in the child table.

issues.evidence: The specification's semantic rule tweets.createdate in 2018 ('createdate >= 2018-01-01 AND < 2019-01-01') is not implemented. DateSampler (values.py) draws from self.full = (1800-01-01, 2100-01-01) or from the compact min/max range, and _constraints_for (instance.py) never passes a date range constraint. The spec's formula_kind only classifies positive/nonneg/nonzero/maxlen, so the date-range formula is silently dropped. Generated createdate values can therefore fall outside 2018.
issues.requested_revision: Add a date-range constraint kind (e.g. 'between' with lo/hi datetimes) to formula_kind and pass it to DateSampler so generated createdate values satisfy 2018-01-01 <= createdate < 2019-01-01, while still planting the required tie for ORDER BY createdate ASC.

issues.evidence: The specification requires follows.f2 comparison_boundary targets 'sample values around 0 (-1, 1) only; f2=0 is forbidden'. load_specification sets spec['comparison_boundary'][('follows','f2')] = [-1, 1], but NumberSampler._draw only uses boundary values with probability 0.25 and otherwise draws uniformly from [min,max] (values.py: full = r.random() < self.p ... v = r.randint(int(lo), int(hi))). The semantic rule f2 <> 0 is classified as 'nonzero' and applied, but the boundary values -1/1 are not guaranteed to appear, and the spec's 'only' wording is not honored. Also, the semantic rule f2 <> 0 is applied via formula_kind, but the boundary list is not enforced as the sole domain.
issues.requested_revision: For follows.f2, restrict the sampler domain to {-1, 1} (or at least guarantee both -1 and 1 appear in every instance) and never emit 0; do not rely on the 0.25 boundary probability. Add a post-write check that f2 values are a subset of {-1, 1} and that both values occur.

issues.evidence: The specification requires user_profiles.followers comparison_boundary 'include values at 1000 and one step below/above'. load_specification sets spec['comparison_boundary'][('user_profiles','followers')] = [1000] (DEFAULT_FOLLOWERS_BOUNDARY), but NumberSampler only uses boundary values with probability 0.25 and does not plant 999/1001. The semantic rule followers >= 0 is applied, but the boundary triple (999, 1000, 1001) is not guaranteed.
issues.requested_revision: Plant 999, 1000 and 1001 explicitly in user_profiles.followers (at least one row each per instance) in addition to the >= 0 rule, and verify post-write that all three values occur.

issues.evidence: The specification requires user_profiles.name comparison_boundary 'include exact Iron Man and a near-typo variant' and like_near_variant 'prefix/near matches for %Swif% style literals'. load_specification maps like_near_variant to DEFAULT_LIKE_LITERALS = ('%int%','%intern%') and DEFAULT_LIKE_VARIANTS for *every* like_near_variant column, including user_profiles.name and user_profiles.email. The name column therefore gets '%int%'/'%intern%' literals instead of '%Swif%' and 'Iron Man', and the comparison_boundary for name is set to DEFAULT_COMPARISON_BOUNDARY = (-1,0,1) (numeric) rather than the string 'Iron Man'.
issues.requested_revision: Make like_literals/like_variants and comparison_boundary per-column and type-aware: for user_profiles.name use '%Swif%' plus near variants and the exact string 'Iron Man' plus a typo variant; for user_profiles.email use '%edu%' and '%supers%' near variants; for tweets.text use '%int%'/'%intern%' with the listed variants. Do not apply numeric boundary values to varchar columns.

issues.evidence: The specification requires user_profiles.uid group_sizes 'groups of size 1, 2 and >=3 across referenced uid children' and tweets.uid group_sizes 'groups of size 1, 2 and >=3'. _apply_group_sizes (instance.py) writes blocks of the target sizes into the column array, but for user_profiles.uid the column is a PK and is overwritten by _fresh_pk_start (sequential integers) after sampling, and for tweets.uid the FK fill (fill_foreign_keys_consistently) and the later _post_verify re-planting can destroy the group-size structure. The post-verify re-applies _apply_group_sizes to tweets.uid, but this overwrites FK values with arbitrary pool values, breaking FK integrity (see issue 1) and not guaranteeing the referenced-child group sizes on user_profiles.uid.
issues.requested_revision: Enforce group_sizes on the *final* arrays: for user_profiles.uid, choose the set of parent keys and the number of children per parent so that child counts hit 1, 2 and >=3, then fill tweets.uid/follows.f1 from that distribution; do not re-plant group sizes on FK columns after FK fill. Verify post-write that the child-count histogram contains 1, 2 and >=3.

issues.evidence: The specification requires user_profiles.uid aggregate_boundary 'COUNT(*) per group in {0,1,2,3}' and tweets.uid aggregate_boundary 'COUNT(*) per group in {0,1,2,3}'. _apply_agg_boundary (instance.py) makes blocks of distinct values of size tgt, but for user_profiles.uid the PK is overwritten by sequential integers, and for tweets.uid the FK fill and post-verify re-planting can destroy the block structure. The '0' target (a group with zero rows) is not achievable by writing values into a column; it requires a parent with no children, which is the unmatched_join_rows case and is not implemented (issue 2).
issues.requested_revision: Implement aggregate_boundary together with unmatched_join_rows: ensure at least one parent has 0 children (COUNT=0), and that child counts 1, 2, 3 occur. Apply on final arrays after FK fill; do not re-plant on FK columns.

issues.evidence: The specification requires user_profiles.partitionid aggregate_boundary 'COUNT(*) per group in {1,2,3}'. _apply_agg_boundary is applied to partitionid, but partitionid is nullable and _plant_nulls runs before _apply_agg_boundary in build_random_instance, and _post_verify re-applies _apply_agg_boundary after _ensure_one_null, which can overwrite the planted NULL or the block structure. The interaction between NULL planting and aggregate-boundary planting is not verified.
issues.requested_revision: Order the steps so NULL planting and aggregate-boundary planting are consistent (e.g. plant NULLs in rows outside the boundary blocks, or count NULL as its own group), and verify post-write that COUNT(*) over partitionid groups takes 1, 2 and 3.

issues.evidence: The specification requires user_profiles.email duplicates_for_distinct '20-50% duplicate share among non-null' and user_profiles.uid/tweets.uid duplicates_for_distinct '20-50%'. _enforce_dup_share (instance.py) is called in _post_verify for columns in spec['dup_share'], but for user_profiles.uid the PK is overwritten by sequential integers after sampling, so the duplicate share is 0; for tweets.uid the FK fill and re-planting can change the share. The post-verify _enforce_dup_share is applied to user_profiles.uid, which would break the PK uniqueness (it copies values into other rows), and then sample_fresh_primary_keys is not re-run after _post_verify.
issues.requested_revision: Do not apply duplicate-share enforcement to primary-key columns (uid, tweets.id). For user_profiles.email and tweets.uid, enforce the 20-50% share on the final arrays after FK fill and verify post-write; for tweets.uid, ensure the duplicate share is achieved by repeating existing parent keys, not by inventing new ones.

issues.evidence: The specification requires tweets.id aggregate_boundary 'COUNT(id) values 0,1,2,3' and null_in_count_column/null_rows 'no NULL (NOT NULL)'. _apply_agg_boundary is applied to tweets.id, but tweets.id is a PK and is overwritten by _fresh_pk_start (sequential integers) after sampling, so the block structure is destroyed. The '0' target is not achievable by writing values into a NOT NULL PK column.
issues.requested_revision: For tweets.id, the aggregate_boundary targets should be interpreted as COUNT over groups of the *table* (e.g. COUNT(tweets.id) per user), not as values in the id column. Implement by controlling the number of tweets per user (0,1,2,3) together with unmatched_join_rows, and do not re-plant on the PK column.

issues.evidence: The specification requires tweets.createdate ties_for_order_limit 'at least two generated rows share a createdate value'. _apply_ties is applied in _post_verify for columns in spec['ties_order'], but _constraints_for also passes ties to DateSampler only if schema.original_values has non-NULL values for (tweets, createdate). The post-verify _apply_ties copies one value into another row, which is fine, but the DateSampler's 0.30 tie probability and the post-verify both operate; the execution feedback does not report a tie check. The specification's date range (2018) is not enforced (issue 3), so ties may be outside 2018.
issues.requested_revision: After enforcing the 2018 date range, guarantee at least two generated rows share a createdate value within 2018 (post-write check), and keep the tie when re-planting other targets.

issues.evidence: The specification requires user_profiles.followers rows_with_different_values '>=2 rows per comparable group with different followers'. _apply_rows_diff_values (instance.py) only ensures the whole column has >=2 distinct values, not that each comparable group (e.g. per partitionid or per name) has >=2 rows with different followers. The spec's example is 'scalar:SELECT(MAX(user_profiles.followers))' with 'qualifying_rows: >= 2 per group with different values'.
issues.requested_revision: Implement rows_with_different_values per group: for each group (by the grouping column implied by the query, e.g. partitionid), ensure at least two rows have different followers values. Verify post-write.

issues.evidence: The specification requires user_profiles.name group_sizes 'groups of size 1, 2 and >=3' and follows.f1 group_sizes 'groups of size 1, 2 and >=3'. _apply_group_sizes is applied to name and f1, but for follows.f1 the FK fill (fill_foreign_keys_consistently) and the later _post_verify re-planting can destroy the group-size structure; for name, _plant_nulls runs before _apply_group_sizes and _post_verify re-applies _apply_group_sizes after _ensure_one_null, which can overwrite the planted NULL or the block structure. issues.evidence: Spec requires 'follows composite PK collisions must be avoided against compact tuples' and 'exclude one parent key so it stays childless' per (parent,key). That does not satisfy the spec's stronger requirement that at least one parent has zero children in tweets.uid AND at least one parent has zero children in follows.f1 independently — but this is minor since the same key being childless in both is still valid. However, composite-PK collision with compact tuples is not enforced: the writer's `_existing_keys` check will drop generated follows rows whose (f1,f2) tuple repeats a compact tuple, reducing the realized counts below the planned 0/1/2/>=3 histogram and the required size of 10, silently skewing the group_sizes/unmatched_join targets.
